PAGE 2
Gerry Conway, the writer who co-created the Punisher and forever shook Spider-Man's status quo by penning the tragic death of Gwen Stacy, died April 26, 2026. Born Sept. 10, 1952, Conway was only 18 years old when he began working on Amazing Spider-Man, following Stan Lee as the series' regular writer. His run on Amazing Spider-Man from issues #111-149 (Aug. 1972 to Oct. 1975) broke new ground for the character. His storylines included 'The Night Gwen Stacy Died' in Amazing Spider-Man #121, the introduction of the Jackal's spider-clone in Amazing Spider-Man #151 and the Punisher's first appearance in Amazing Spider-Man #129. He co-created characters Man-Thing, Werewolf by Night and the Jackal, and he gave Carol Danvers her first super-heroic identity as Ms. Marvel. He also had significant achievements at DC Comics, and has written almost every super hero at both companies. But Conway wasn't limited to one medium, writing science fiction novels (Midnight Dancers and Mindship) and co-writing film scripts with Roy Thomas (Conan the Destroyer and Fire & Ice). For many years he wrote for television and became a consulting producer of Hercules, executive producer of The Huntress and co-executive producer of Law & Order: Criminal Intent. He would return to Marvel in recent decades, writing Carnage, Amazing Spider-Man: Renew Your Vows and more. Outspoken and accomplished, Conway created a powerful legacy in comics and will be missed by all who knew him and his work.

'From Spider-Man to the Avengers, Iron Man to Captain Marvel, Gerry Conway has deftly written almost every character in the Marvel Universe. He thrilled us with new characters like the Punisher and broke our hearts in emotional tales like 'The Night Gwen Stacy Died,' a story that affects Spider-Man to this day. Whether in the pages of Marvel's comics or on the big screen in our films, Gerry Conway had an undeniable and indelible impact on the super hero stories we know and love.' — C.B. CEBULSKI, EDITOR IN CHIEF

PAGE 3
Address me again. By name.

My full name.

Sir. General George Washington, sir, commander in chief of the Continental Army of the United Colonies.

1775. July.

And the year?

The Siege of Boston. The British have taken the city but have thus far been prevented from moving farther: a stalemate.

You wish for me to defeat them, then travel to Philadelphia to the Second Continental Conference, to both draft and sign a full Declaration of Independence by July 4th of next year--

--thereby formalizing a state of war between the Thirteen Colonies and the British Empire.

You then wish for me to win this war, securing your liberty.

That, uh...

...that would be ideal, sir.

PAGE 4
I understand. Leave me alone. Doom must plan.

You heard General Washington: The British doom must be planned! Give him his space!

My mind, in the body of the American General Washington. This...

...this presents a unique opportunity.

Doom has mastered all disciplines, including the study of lesser nations: One must always know one's enemy.

what originally happens here is as follows:

Arriving at this camp, Washington realizes he must impose discipline on these 'patriots,' to turn them from a volunteer militia into an organized army.

At the same time, he must find a way to expel the British from Boston.

He enlists the help of young Henry Knox. Knox dissuades him from invading immediately, instead convincing him to let the siege draw out for months...

...so Knox can travel to New York, where recently captured heavy artillery lay.

Knox--alongside his horses and men--drag these sixty tons of mortars and cannons behind them for three months, across three hundred miles of winter terrain, to reach Boston.

It is a significant act of logistics.

The fortifications are installed and used...

...and after a bombardment from a distance their cannons cannot reach, the British choose to flee.

It is an early, decisive and influential American victory.

A lesser man would do all he could to ensure such a delicate moment in history remains intact. But while the enemies of Doom have many words to describe me...

...'lesser' is not among them.

There is another path, if I can realize it: as bold, as singular and as unprecedented as Doom himself.

It promises a challenge.

It promises glory.

PAGE 5
Born to a poor nomad and an ill-fated witch, VICTOR VON DOOM used his talent for combining sorcery and technology to take over the European country of Latveria, making him one of the most formidable individuals on the planet. Over the years, Doom has wielded his power for great good and great evil, leaving the people of Earth with one question to ponder and fear: What will Doctor Doom do next?

REED RICHARDS, scientist and leader of the FANTASTIC FOUR, proposed a new form of time travel in which a powerful mind could harness and alter pivotal moments in history in a single instant. Doom used Reed's idea to create the DOOM ENGINE to rewrite history in Latveria's favor. To stop him from activating the machine, Reed sent Doom back in time to the sinking of the RMS TITANIC and trapped him in a time loop. Doom discovered if his host body died or if a threshold of sufficient changes to history was met, the loop would restart and could only be severed by blocking his re-entry point and being drawn to a random point in history. Before exiting the loop, Doom took the Titanic hostage and negotiated for aid to be sent to Latveria, securing the country's future success. He then traversed through time once more, inhabiting the body of GENERAL GEORGE WASHINGTON at the start of the Revolutionary War!

PAGE 6
I would speak to Knox.

He is I, General Washington, sir! What can I do for you?

There are weapons in New York.

Fort Ticonderoga, yes.

Captured just two months ago by Benedict Arnold--a great patriot, sir.

I would have them. You must leave immediately.

I thought--it was my understanding you wanted to attack?

No longer, not at once. Supplies are needed.

I will find a way to bring those artillery here, sir--though it may take months, I swear I'll--

Not just the weapons.

On your way you are to liberate these supplies from all who have them.

You're--

You're building a forge, sir?

And a lab and an arsenal. We are to build weapons, and supplies are needed.

But--the cannons at Ticonderoga are weapons, superior to--

They are inferior to what I will craft...

...after they have been melted down and reforged into new alloys.

If you don't mind me asking, sir, what do you intend to forge?

Two items, Knox.

One is a weapon, to attack with a might not yet seen on Earth...

PAGE 7
...and the other is armor.

PAGE 8
Knox pulls what I require across a young nation to me.

He is a useful man: as loyal and idealistic as he is submissive to my authority.

He throws his whole body into accomplishing the task I have set before him.

And I begin forging them into what I require.

First: a weapon faster, more accurate--and more devastating--than anything else on the planet:

A rotary cannon--and the ammunition it requires.

Such a weapon demands technologies that will not normally be invented for hundreds of years--

--but that means defenses against it are similarly distant.

There are some concessions required to be made to current technology, true...

...but even those are not without their appeal.

Which brings me to my armor.

Even without its usual electronics--and, due to the weight of its materials, without its usual capability of flight--

--I find that it has a remarkable style--and charm.

Doom can work wonders, even with steam.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- KLANG
- KSSSSSSTTT

PAGE 9
And thus, in just a few months, General George Washington of the United Colonies has all he requires.

Knox, Gather the men. Inform them we are to confront the British.

The largest and most powerful empire this planet has ever known is about to fall.

PAGE 10
An address is required.

Men: I have asked your patience, lo these past months. But I know you have all been curious. The noises--the machinery. What is he building in there?

I trust that curiosity is now satisfied. I have willed the glories I require into existence. They stand before you.

And while I alone control these great technologies...

...I do not ask of you anything I do not offer myself.

You are all volunteers, and volunteers you shall remain. You may rest here if you wish: My victory will still be your victory. But if you choose to follow me into battle--

--either to witness or to satisfy your own bloodlust against the hated British in my wake--

--know that you are free to do so.

For as I finally have all I need to drive the invaders from these shores...

...we shall do so tonight!

PAGE 11
And thus, we bring the war to the British. Their front lines show confidence.

Look! Finally, the traitors come to meet their deaths!

They jest, unaware and thus unafraid of what it is that comes at them...

...but their reinforcements will enjoy no such privilege.

No! Impossible!

stand your ground, men! Kill this rabble!

Howe, sir--it's Washington! He's made a weapon beyond all!

Poppycock. He could never. Washington is a mere surveyor, not a weaponsmith, and--

You would do well to learn, General...

SOUND EFFECTS:
- PING
- PING
- PING
- WHHHH
- Rarrrghh!
- BRATATATATATATATATATATATATATATAT
- KABOOM

PAGE 12
...that Washington is whoever I choose him to be.

We have use of their ships, men!

Leave them unharmed!

It is victory in her purest form: complete, unequivocal--

--and glorious.

The men insist on a celebration--in a recently liberated Bostonian tavern.

Washington, the great orator! Favor us with your words!

Yes! Speech! Speech!

Listen to this, Robertson. Washington never disappoints.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- BRR
- ATAT ATATAT AT ATAT ATAT
- RARRRGHHHHH!

PAGE 13
"The British Empire." "The United Colonies." They are all the same.

You are all the same.

You think yourselves exceptional by dint of assuming an identity so new it is still being manufactured.

You fool no one.

You bicker about taxation, but both your nations pursue the same lies, worship the same gods, commit the same acts of hate over and over again.

Or have you stopped kidnapping men, women and children from distant shores to force them into labor?

Uh...normally, the General's speeches are much better than this.

But Know this...

...my revolution has only just begun. Drink well, for I will bring this revolution to the Empire!

Know this: Tomorrow, we sail for England! Tomorrow, we sail for Buckingham Palace!

Tomorrow, we sail for total victory!!

Yes! That's more like it!

We must've misunderstood the first part!

PAGE 14
Six weeks at sea. I use the time to reinforce my spellcasting.

Already I can resist my changes to history reaching their threshold and sending me elsewhere.

And it is good, for there is much yet to accomplish for my beloved Latveria.

Though there is much I have achieved even here at sea--including magically increasing my steed's strength.

We fly under a false flag: an English flag. Nobody suspects a thing as we sail, unchallenged, into port.

And by the time they realize something is wrong...

Rue, Britannia.

...they do not live long enough to regret it.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- BRATATTATTT!

PAGE 15
I know the way to their palace. Most of the roads follow the same path in my time.

We fight our way to Britain's heart, taking fire from all sides.

The men alongside me die.

I do not.

Stop him! Someone, stop hiaaaarrrrgggh!

SOUND EFFECTS:
- Rarrgh!
- PING
- PING

PAGE 16
And soon, the head of this empire is within reach. But a warning has already reached them...

Men...

...fire!!!

...and they have had time enough to prepare.

The clamor is almost deafening-- the sound of every impact of every bullet rings in my ears.

But it is not noise. It is a song.

And I am its conductor.

You believe you are ready for me. You, as is your eternal custom, wrong.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- BOOOOM
- PING
- PING
- PING
- PING
- SWAT

PAGE 17
The symphony of violence that comes next passes as if in a blur.

Certain images stand out, but the ultimate conclusion to the revolution--

--to my revolution--

--is as certain as it is satisfying.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- KRA-KOOM
- BRAKAKAKAK
- FA-SMACK
- WHAM

PAGE 18
Then, after some acts of consolidation, all that remains is to inform the world of my ascendency.

This empire--your empire--now falls to me. And should you discover you disagree...

...you are free to attack me at your peril.

Are--is England to be the fourteenth colony, Supreme Lord Washington?

Don't be a fool. The colonies no longer exist. Neither, for that matter, does the British Empire and her 'possessions.' Both have been annexed by the country you now serve, for they are all now a part of Greater Latveria.

Let all who would interfere with Latveria know that they now interfere with an empire whose memory is long...

...whose ultimate bounds nature has not yet ascertained...

...and upon whom the sun does not set.

There may soon come a time when I--Washington--claim to have no knowledge of these events. But Know this: The treaties I have signed are watertight, the wealth I have transferred irreversible.

And you have all and will all be richly rewarded for sustaining this new order here.

Long live Latveria.

PAGE 19
My great work here complete, I release my spellcasting. A snap-like pull...

...and I find myself once again traveling through time--through history itself.

Alongside Titanic, another change is now chambered in my magnificent time engine.

Soon--by all pulling in the same direction at once--these changes will be significant enough to force history into a new preferred shape...

...where Latveria is dominant.

It is true that I cannot choose my next destination--but it is equally true that I do not need to.

For wherever and whenever I land, whoever I possess...

...Doom will be triumphant.

And as goes Doom...

...so goes Latveria.

SOUND EFFECTS:
- BY-KSH

PAGE 20
Suddenly, I find myself on my back, in darkness...

Rargh!

...with someone's head resting contentedly against my shoulder.

What's the matter? Why do you stir?

I--

I need light.

You'll remember there's a lantern outside, though I'm sure you'll also remember we extinguished it for a reason.

I will light it and return.

If you insist.

But make haste, darling. I don't want to spend any more time apart from you than I have to...

PAGE 21
...now that you are officially the Victor of my heart.

Valeria?!

SIGNS AND LABELS:
- NEXT: VALERIA?!

PAGE 22
Doom finds his consciousness within the body of his CHILDHOOD SELF. But now, with the knowledge of what is to come, Doom has a chance to do things differently--and BETTER. It's a journey to the center of Victor Von Doom himself as he discovers how wildly differently his life could've gone...and the price he must pay to keep such victories...

SIGNS AND LABELS:
- DOOMQUEST

text.full_text:
Born to a poor nomad and an ill-fated witch, VICTOR VON DOOM used his talent for combining sorcery and technology to take over the European country of Latveria, making him one of the most formidable individuals on the planet. Over the years, Doom has wielded his power for great good and great evil, leaving the people of Earth with one question to ponder and fear: What will Doctor Doom do next?
DOOMQUEST
REED RICHARDS, scientist and leader of the FANTASTIC FOUR, proposed a new form of time travel in which a powerful mind could harness and alter pivotal moments in history in a single instant. Doom used Reed's idea to create the DOOM ENGINE to rewrite history in Latveria's favor. To stop him from activating the machine, Reed sent Doom back in time to the sinking of the RMS TITANIC and trapped him in a time loop. Doom discovered if his host body died or if a threshold of sufficient changes to history was met, the loop would restart and could only be severed by blocking his re-entry point and being drawn to a random point in history. Before exiting the loop, Doom took the Titanic hostage and negotiated for aid to be sent to Latveria, securing the country's future success. He then traversed through time once more, inhabiting the body of GENERAL GEORGE WASHINGTON at the start of the Revolutionary War!

text.full_text: Suddenly, I find myself on my back, in darkness... Rargh! ...with someone's head resting contentedly against my shoulder. What's the matter? Why do you stir? I-- I need light. You'll remember there's a lantern outside, though I'm sure you'll also remember we extinguished it for a reason. I will light it and return. If you insist. But make haste, darling. I don't want to spend any more time apart from you than I have to...
